title: Types of breeding:
text:
Types of breeding:

1. Inbreeding – breeding of related animals.
2. Outbreeding – breeding of unrelated animals.
   a. Cross breeding – mating of two animals of different breeds. Superior traits that result in the crossbred progeny from crossbreeding are called hybrid vigor or heterosis.

Bull of breed A (100%)
Cow of breed B (100%)
F1 crossbred progeny 50% A and 50% B

b. Upgrading - is the breeding of animals of two different breeds where the animals of an indigenous breed/genetic group is mated by an improved pure breed for several generations towards attaining the superior traits of the improved breed.

Imported breed
Native breed
Upgraded

facts: Inbreeding is defined as the breeding of related animals.
Outbreeding is defined as the breeding of unrelated animals.
Cross breeding is the mating of two animals of different breeds.
Superior traits that result in crossbred progeny from crossbreeding are referred to as hybrid vigor or heterosis.
Mating a Bull of breed A (100%) with a Cow of breed B (100%) yields F1 crossbred progeny with 50% breed A and 50% breed B.
Upgrading is the breeding of animals of two different breeds where animals of an indigenous breed or genetic group are mated to an improved pure breed for several generations.
The primary goal of upgrading is attaining the superior traits of the improved breed in the resulting stock.
In upgrading, an imported or improved pure breed is bred with a native or indigenous breed to produce an upgraded animal.
